intro.quote: RSVP soft state is created and periodically refreshed by Path and Resv messages. The state is deleted if no matching refresh messages arrive before the expiration of a "cleanup timeout" interval.

steps.explain: The sender periodically sends a Path message for the data flow it originates.

cite.quote: Each sender host periodically sends a Path message for each data flow it originates.

steps.explain: The receiver sends a reservation request upstream, hop by hop, toward the sender along the reverse data path.

cite.quote: Resv messages carry reservation requests hop-by-hop from receivers to senders, along the reverse paths of data flows for the session.

intro.quote: To request a confirmation for its reservation request, a receiver Rj includes in the Resv message a confirmation-request object containing Rj's IP address.

steps.explain: The upstream node sends a ResvConf to the receiver as a probabilistic acknowledgement of the reservation request.

cite.quote: ResvConf messages are sent to (probabilistically) acknowledge reservation requests.

intro.quote: ResvErr (reservation error) messages report errors in processing Resv messages, or they may report the spontaneous disruption of a reservation, e.g., by administrative preemption.

steps.explain: The node that detected the error reports it downstream to the appropriate receiver using reservation state.

cite.quote: ResvErr messages travel downstream towards the appropriate receivers, routed hop-by-hop using the reservation state.

intro.quote: RSVP "teardown" messages remove path or reservation state immediately.

steps.explain: A sender can initiate a PathTear that travels downstream and removes matching path state.

cite.quote: PathTear messages are initiated explicitly by senders or by path state timeout in any node, and they travel downstream towards all receivers.

steps.explain: The receiver initiates a ResvTear that travels upstream and removes matching reservation state.

cite.quote: ResvTear messages are initiated explicitly by receivers or by any node in which reservation state has timed out, and they travel upstream towards all matching senders.

intro.quote: An RSVP message consists of a common header, followed by a body consisting of a variable number of variable-length, typed "objects".

fields.name: Vers
fields.explain: Specifies the RSVP protocol version; this specification defines version 1.

cite.quote: Vers: 4 bits Protocol version number. This is version 1.

fields.name: Flags
fields.explain: Carries flag bits, none of which are defined in this version.

cite.quote: Flags: 4 bits 0x01-0x08: Reserved No flag bits are defined yet.

fields.name: Msg Type
fields.explain: Identifies the RSVP message type, such as Path or Resv.

cite.quote: Msg Type: 8 bits 1 = Path 2 = Resv

fields.name: RSVP Checksum
fields.explain: Protects the message with a one's-complement checksum; an all-zero value means that no checksum was transmitted.

cite.quote: RSVP Checksum: 16 bits The one's complement of the one's complement sum of the message, with the checksum field replaced by zero for the purpose of computing the checksum. An all-zero value means that no checksum was transmitted.

fields.name: Send_TTL
fields.explain: Records the IP TTL value used when the message was sent.

cite.quote: Send_TTL: 8 bits The IP TTL value with which the message was sent. See Section 3.8.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.explain: An eight-bit area is reserved in the common header.

cite.quote: |  Send_TTL   | (Reserved)  |        RSVP Length        |

fields.name: RSVP Length
fields.explain: Gives the total message length in bytes, including the common header and the variable-length objects that follow.

cite.quote: RSVP Length: 16 bits The total length of this RSVP message in bytes, including the common header and the variable-length objects that follow.

intro.quote: Every object consists of one or more 32-bit words with a one-word header, with the following format:

fields.name: Length
fields.explain: Gives the total object length in bytes; the length must be a multiple of four and at least four.

cite.quote: Length A 16-bit field containing the total object length in bytes. Must always be a multiple of 4, and at least 4.

fields.name: Class-Num
fields.explain: Identifies the object's class.

cite.quote: Class-Num Identifies the object class; values of this field are defined in Appendix A.

fields.name: C-Type
fields.explain: Identifies the object type within its class.

cite.quote: C-Type Object type, unique within Class-Num. Values are defined in Appendix A.

fields.name: Object contents
fields.explain: Carries the type-specific contents of the object.

cite.quote: (Object contents)

intro.quote: The format of a Path message is as follows:

fields.name: Common Header
fields.explain: The common header at the start of the Path message.

cite.quote: <Path Message> ::= <Common Header> [ <INTEGRITY> ]

fields.name: INTEGRITY
fields.explain: Provides optional integrity data placed immediately after the common header.

cite.quote: If the INTEGRITY object is present, it must immediately follow the common header.

fields.name: SESSION
fields.explain: Identifies the session by destination address, protocol identifier, and generalized destination port.

cite.quote: SESSION Contains the IP destination address (DestAddress), the IP protocol id, and some form of generalized destination port, to define a specific session for the other objects that follow. Required in every RSVP message.

fields.name: RSVP_HOP
fields.explain: Carries the sending node's address and a logical outgoing interface handle.

cite.quote: RSVP_HOP Carries the IP address of the RSVP-capable node that sent this message and a logical outgoing interface handle (LIH; see Section 3.3).

fields.name: TIME_VALUES
fields.explain: Carries the refresh period used to generate the message and is required in every Path message.

cite.quote: TIME_VALUES Contains the value for the refresh period R used by the creator of the message; see Section 3.7. Required in every Path and Resv message.

fields.name: POLICY_DATA
fields.explain: Carries policy information for a local policy module and may appear in a Path message.

cite.quote: POLICY_DATA Carries information that will allow a local policy module to decide whether an associated reservation is administratively permitted. May appear in Path, Resv, PathErr, or ResvErr message.

fields.name: SENDER_TEMPLATE
fields.explain: Identifies the sender and is required in a Path message.

cite.quote: SENDER_TEMPLATE Contains a sender IP address and perhaps some additional demultiplexing information to identify a sender. Required in a Path message.

fields.name: SENDER_TSPEC
fields.explain: Describes the sender's traffic characteristics and is required in a Path message.

cite.quote: SENDER_TSPEC Defines the traffic characteristics of a sender's data flow. Required in a Path message.

fields.name: ADSPEC
fields.explain: Carries OPWA advertising data in a Path message.

cite.quote: ADSPEC Carries OPWA data, in a Path message.

intro.quote: The Resv message format is as follows:

fields.name: Common Header
fields.explain: The common header at the start of the Resv message.

cite.quote: <Resv Message> ::= <Common Header> [ <INTEGRITY> ]

fields.name: INTEGRITY
fields.explain: Provides optional integrity data placed immediately after the common header.

cite.quote: If the INTEGRITY object is present, it must immediately follow the common header.

fields.name: SESSION
fields.explain: Identifies the session by destination address, protocol identifier, and generalized destination port.

cite.quote: SESSION Contains the IP destination address (DestAddress), the IP protocol id, and some form of generalized destination port, to define a specific session for the other objects that follow. Required in every RSVP message.

fields.name: TIME_VALUES
fields.explain: Carries the refresh period used to generate the message and is required in every Resv message.

cite.quote: TIME_VALUES Contains the value for the refresh period R used by the creator of the message; see Section 3.7. Required in every Path and Resv message.

fields.name: RESV_CONFIRM
fields.explain: Requests a reservation confirmation and carries the receiver address to which the ResvConf should be sent.

cite.quote: The appearance of a RESV_CONFIRM object signals a request for a reservation confirmation and carries the IP address of the receiver to which the ResvConf should be sent.

fields.name: SCOPE
fields.explain: Carries an explicit list of sender hosts toward which the message is forwarded.

cite.quote: SCOPE Carries an explicit list of sender hosts towards which the information in the message is to be forwarded. May appear in a Resv, ResvErr, or ResvTear message. See Section 3.4.

fields.name: POLICY_DATA
fields.explain: Carries policy information for a local policy module and may appear in a Resv message.

cite.quote: POLICY_DATA Carries information that will allow a local policy module to decide whether an associated reservation is administratively permitted. May appear in Path, Resv, PathErr, or ResvErr message.

fields.name: STYLE
fields.explain: Defines the reservation style and its style-specific options; it is required in every Resv message.

cite.quote: STYLE Defines the reservation style plus style-specific information that is not in FLOWSPEC or FILTER_SPEC objects. Required in every Resv message.

fields.name: flow descriptor list
fields.explain: Carries a style-dependent list of flow descriptors.

cite.quote: The BNF above defines a flow descriptor list as simply a list of flow descriptors.
